name: Should a landlord hire a handyman or a general contractor for rental repairs?

mainEntity.name: Should a landlord hire a handyman or a general contractor for rental repairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hiring an owner-operated general contractor provides a single point of contact for complex, multi-trade repairs, whereas a standard handyman is best for isolated, minor tasks. If a rental requires drywall work, tile replacement, finish carpentry, and coordinated electrical or plumbing sub-trades, a general contractor keeps the schedule organized. For just tightening loose hardware or swapping a single faucet, an independent handyman may be sufficient. Choosing a contractor avoids the hassle of managing separate workers across multiple trades.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a handyman for quick, isolated fixes. Hire an owner-operated general contractor when the rental needs multi-trade work, such as drywall, tile, carpentry, and coordinated trades.
